Here are the 1000 words! Remember that your hamster's name is Gucci. It was a pet name that matched his fur. I loved that name, because it was nice and small. One day I was leaving work, and I walked in to the bathroom. I was quickly overcome with the smell of his absence; his little torture chamber was empty. I walked into the closet, and I could hear his whirring. He had run out of food in his bowl just that morning. His water had been drained. His blanket was shredded to a thread. He was kind of a ridiculous hamster, but I found him time and time again, sometimes even finding food and treats in his tunnel and clawing them down. I had to heartlessly leave him with a neighbor, as he seemed to have based his view of the world very shortly after I got him. I tried not to think about it too much, which stoked my idealization of him even more. I know, he was just a pet rat. He couldn't have had any effect on my life. Right? 
Right?

I started to remember here and there how often he would play with us in our backyard and inside the house, and all the things he did with us. That fucking ham became a part of family.
•
Growing up, his presence was just something about him that was always around. Mark was constantly building tunnels and filling his water and food dishes. When he died, everyone's grief was equal, but then most of us were such pets ourselves that we noticed it less to the average person. 
•
We found that sleeping in our hammocks during a thunderstorm somehow made us feel closer to each other. Along with naming your hamster 'Gameraman', I wasn't sure how to process the mourning and decided to opiate in corner of my bedroom instead. I came back early this winter from work at 6am as he should have been getting ready for his bed. There's a clock in my bedroom telling time, which I faced away from to avoid it scaring me. It reads:
11:54
But that meant he had been awake for 3 hours, huddling up in bed with a coat of Polish fur. His wheel hadn't been rotated at all during his attempt to escape regardless of his paw infection. I just couldn't face him with it. It slithered away at the back of is cage and hopped into the far corner.  
•
His birthday was coming up on April 14th. It's three days after mine. That was over a week away now. Today, I still sleep in my grandson's room. I slept there before my husband and my two youngest boys were on Vacation. He turned 7 on my birthdate. Easter came up a few days later, and his only present then was a few crackers. Easter wasn't a big thing in my family, but Mark was always curious during my Holiday preparations, as I'd always clean out his cage on his day. I had a dingy Old-School common bed with a little triangle edge’d railing to hold off on falls. I lifeguarded the bedroom and didn't give him access to the biggest side of the bed, and let him take the smaller side. He sat quietly with me, and if I tried to tilt so he could get Trading Places on the other pee-keylight, he’d slyly wink at me. I still live in his sprawled out, hairy little world. He may have been a screw-up, and his lies made things worse for me. He just liked the complexity of me. He'd always sleep at night right beside my bed. Whenever we’d play, he would curl up beside me, resting when it was my turn to blow a huge fire on him.
I didn’t understand it, but he found a single spot in the sun. A vantage point. We’d sit awning to awning like that.
•
And then he started feeling less snuggly when we were playing. More intermittent and less cuddly. I suddenly noticed he was threading more challenges. Our work hadn’t seemed like so much of a burden before. That damn fucking goddamn guttencaster. It wasn’t like he was getting ornery with us. I was going to put him in the kitchen again. He kept my peace in the kitchen. I was gradually becoming mad at him.
Am I Iggy Poetta here?
Have you had a bad lab rat? Some of us only have pet hamsters......
